entry.title: The Merck/Moderna Results
entry.summary:
This is one of those times - and there are many - when you should evaluate a biopharma news story based on the science and not on the stock market. I’m referring to the clinical trial data that Merck and Moderna released yesterday for their vaccine (intismeran autogene)/Keytruda combination in melanoma patients after surgery. That should probably read “released under duress”, because the data leaked in advance of a meeting presentation, and the companies were more or less forced to press-release on the numbers.

Source: In the Pipeline (Derek Lowe — Drug Discovery & Chemistry) · Tags: #genomics-proteins #materials-science

entry.title: HYphlow: bringing end-to-end flow to HyPhy selection analyses, from taxon reconciliation to trait-based foreground assignment
entry.summary:
Phylogenetic analyses of molecular evolution often require repeated manual preparation to reconcile taxa, annotate trees, execute models, and summarize results. These steps become increasingly time-consuming and difficult to standardize as the number of taxa, genes, and analytical hypotheses increases. We present HYphlow, an open-source graphical workflow developed in Python that integrates data preparation, trait-based foreground branch assignment, HyPhy execution, and structured result extraction within a single interface.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus #combinatorics

entry.title: DoAggregate: a pipeline for aggregation testing for rare-variant on a gene and pathway level
entry.summary:
Motivation Aggregation tests overcome the classical limitation of rare variant analysis in cohort study design. Choosing the right statistical test remains one of the biggest challenges. Existing tools fall short in offering a comprehensive solution that includes automatic data processing, testing across all genes, as well as exploration of broader genetic regions such as pathways and Gene Ontology (GO) terms.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: scSTEC: Annotating Chromatin Subcompartments from Individual Single-Cell Hi-C Data via Direct Two-Dimensional Embedding and Chromosome-wise Consensus
entry.summary:
textbf{Motivation: }Single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) technologies enable the study of three-dimensional (3D) genome organization at individual-cell resolution. Many computational methods have been developed to infer hierarchical structures from scHi-C data. However, annotating chromatin subcompartments from sparse scHi-C data remains a challenge.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

entry.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01068-9 The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

entry.title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes

Across three benchmarks, HDM demonstrates increased accuracy and robustness in modeling large protein assemblies, compared with state-of-the-art…
